clue.text: Nothing Henry swapped for a sweet

indicators.note: one letter is exchanged for another, so the henry's letter gives way to the clue's a

parts.note: nothing is a nought, a zero
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone trades away nothing much, Henry, in return for a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapped for' tells you to replace the H in NOUGHT with A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Blokes I employed to fashion a monument

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Men are hired to build a memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone pillar, commonly set up as a monument.

clue.text: Note: pay attention to gloss

parts.note: G is a musical note
to listen is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Memo: take care over the shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gloss' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a sheen.
explanation.definitionFit: A glisten is a sparkling shine, the same thing as a gloss or lustre.

clue.text: Characters in Capitol used to dealing with current affairs

indicators.note: the characters in a word are its letters, taken here as raw material
used means those letters are put to work again in another order

explanation.surface: Figures in Washington's Capitol are accustomed to handling the news of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people, but it means the letters of CAPITOL, which are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical things concern events of present interest, which is what current affairs are.

clue.text: Give send-off to expedition

definitions.meaning: to send someone or something off on its way
speed or promptness in getting something done

explanation.surface: Someone is waved off on a journey of exploration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' looks like a journey, but here it means speed, as in 'with all expedition'.
explanation.definitionFit: To despatch is to send off; despatch as a noun is also haste, the old sense of expedition.

clue.text: Fan seen more where club starts reaching peak

parts.note: extra means more, additional

indicators.note: starts means only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A supporter is seen more often where the club begins to reach the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like a supporter, but it is an extractor fan that draws out air.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor is a fan that removes stale air or fumes from a room.

clue.text: A bird confined in a bottle is restricted in scope

indicators.note: confined in means these pieces are held inside the bottle

parts.note: a phial is a small bottle
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A bird trapped in a bottle has limited room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confined in' is the container signal: the article and the legendary bird go inside the small bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochial means narrow in outlook, limited to a small parish of interest.

clue.text: Understanding shout of encouragement during ecstasy

indicators.note: during means the cheer comes in the middle of the trance

parts.note: a trance is a state of rapture or ecstasy
ole is the Spanish cheer of encouragement

explanation.surface: Sympathy is shown by a cheer at a moment of rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the container signal: the Spanish bullring cheer sits inside the word for rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is a forbearing acceptance of others, an understanding attitude.

clue.text: Giant wrestler asks yacht to move

indicators.note: to move the letters is to shift them into new places

explanation.surface: A huge grappler requests that a boat be shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: Giant Haystacks was a famous British TV wrestler of the 1970s and 80s, a man of enormous size.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant Haystacks was the ring name of a British professional wrestler, Martin Ruane.

clue.text: Even I can appear to be a strange creature

parts.note: even and yet both intensify a comparison: even more, yet more

explanation.surface: Even I could pass for some weird beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the abominable snowman of Himalayan legend, a strange and unproven creature.

clue.text: Finished speaking as a minister

parts.note: something finished is past, over and done
speaking means by word of mouth

explanation.surface: A clergyman has finished preaching his sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister of a church, so acting pastorally is acting in a minister's role.

clue.text: Method for transposing signals

parts.note: a racecourse bookmakers' system of hand and arm signals used to pass changing odds across the course

explanation.surface: A code for relaying messages from one place to another.
explanation.walkthrough: On British racecourses, bookmakers' assistants relayed betting odds by a system of white-gloved hand signals; 'transposing' here means carrying the information across.
explanation.definitionFit: Tic-tac is the semaphore-like signalling used by bookmakers to communicate odds at race meetings.

clue.text: Thanks motoring organisation — vehicle back in the game

indicators.note: back tells you to read the whole run of pieces from end to start

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation
a cab is a taxi, a vehicle

explanation.surface: After thanking the breakdown service, someone gets their car back and returns to the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns all three pieces at once: TA + RAC + CAB reads TARACCAB, which reversed gives the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game, so it is the game the clue points to.

clue.text: Miser gives nothing back to female, having no money around

indicators.note: around means the broke word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: skint is British slang for broke, having no money

indicators.note: back means the word for nothing is read in reverse

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted man gives a woman nothing in return, being broke anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for nothing and 'around' wraps the slang for broke round it and the female letter; 'gives' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a stingy person who hates spending, which is what a miser is.

clue.text: Entertainments aboard ship that's almost the way to do it

indicators.note: aboard means the other pieces are carried inside the ship

parts.note: SS is short for steamship

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: id est, Latin for that is, the full form of i.e.
how means the way or method of doing something

explanation.surface: Fairground acts on a ship cry that's nearly the way to do it, in Punch's catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ID EST to IDES; with HOW it sits inside SS, the steamship abbreviation: S(IDES HOW)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideshows are minor attractions at a fair or circus, entertainments beside the main event.

clue.text: Scholar translated into simple vernacular

indicators.note: translated in its sense of carried across, so the scholar is moved inside

parts.note: simple in the sense of foolish, idiotic
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: An academic renders a text into plain everyday language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' suggests languages, but here it means carried across, so the graduate's letters move inside the word for foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic language uses the natural expressions of native speakers, the everyday vernacular.

clue.text: Anticipate loss of control of aircraft after warning

indicators.note: after places the aircraft's stall behind the warning cry

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
a stall is when a plane loses lift and control

explanation.surface: Predict a plane going out of control once the alarm has sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fore!' is shouted on a golf course to warn others of a ball in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in advance to prevent something, so to anticipate it.

clue.text: By and large, where to find water

definitions.meaning: the main is the open sea, so at sea

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, the place to look for water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means mostly or generally; read literally it means out on the main, the high sea.

clue.text: Greek using sarcastic language? That's not right

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for right must be left out

parts.note: ironic speech says the opposite of what is meant, often with sarcasm

explanation.surface: Is a Greek speaking sarcastically? No, that is not correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not right' looks like a verdict on the guess, but it tells you to remove R from IRONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic means of Ionia, the ancient Greek region, as in the Ionic order of columns.

clue.text: Horse has thrown rider

indicators.note: thrown suggests the letters tumble and land in a different order

explanation.surface: A horse has thrown its rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is not the animal but a clothes horse, a frame for drying laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse is a frame on which laundry is hung to dry, so it is a drier.

clue.text: Ploughmen without time for books

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the ploughmen's word goes round the time unit

parts.note: tillers are people who till or plough the soil
HR, short for hour, is a unit of time

explanation.surface: Farmhands have no time left for reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of outside, so the ploughmen wrap the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrillers are exciting novels of crime or suspense, a class of books.

clue.text: Conservative leader abandons five on way to hearing

indicators.note: abandons means that letter leaves the word for five

parts.note: cinque is five, from the French, used for the five on dice and cards

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A Tory chief walks out on five people heading to a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' removes the Conservative's initial from the French five, as on dice; 'on' sets the street abbreviation after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An inquest is an official judicial inquiry, a hearing into the cause of a death.

clue.text: Rest of flower garlands needing running water

parts.note: leis are Hawaiian garlands of flowers
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Wreaths of flowers that need watering are what is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' looks like the remainder, but it means relaxation; 'running water' is a river, the Yorkshire Ure.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time for relaxation, a period of rest.

clue.text: In a way, I do housework for Mr Hannay

indicators.note: In means the following pieces are placed inside the road

parts.note: RD is short for road, a way
to char is to work as a cleaner

explanation.surface: Somehow, I do the cleaning for a man called Hannay.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Hannay is the hero of John Buchan's The Thirty-Nine Steps. 'In a way' looks like 'somewhat', but 'In' is the container signal round the road abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard is the first name of Hannay, the adventurer in John Buchan's spy novels.

clue.text: See terms here differently to one in America

indicators.note: differently means the given letters are set out in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Notice how terms in British schools are handled differently from those in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' stands for a term: an American college year is split into semesters rather than terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year period of teaching, the usual division of the American academic year.

clue.text: Carpenter needed something obtained from a tree

definitions.meaning: Peter ... is the carpenter among the rustic players in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
a hard yellow fruit grown on a small tree

explanation.surface: A woodworker needed some timber from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The carpenter is a Shakespeare character, not a trade: Peter Quince in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Quince is Shakespeare's carpenter, and a quince is a pear-shaped fruit from a tree.

clue.text: Prevail in conflict about weapon

indicators.note: letters in conflict are at odds and jumbled out of their usual order

parts.note: a lance is a long spear, a weapon

explanation.surface: Someone wins a dispute over arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conflict' is the anagram signal on 'about'; 'weapon' then supplies the knight's spear at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To outbalance is to outweigh, so to win out or prevail over something else.

clue.text: State without a heroic heart

indicators.note: heart means the letters sit in the middle of the run of words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A nation that lacks a brave spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' looks like part of the description, but it points to letters inside 'without a heroic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Young animal has to extract liquid from fish

parts.note: to suck is to draw liquid out with the mouth
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A youngster has to draw its drink from a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A suckling is a baby animal still fed on its mother's milk.

clue.text: With it, shot goes into goal? On the contrary

indicators.note: goes into suggests one piece entering another
On the contrary reverses the insertion just described, so the goal word holds the shot word instead

parts.note: a shot is an attempt, a try
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: With it, a shot ends up in the goal; or rather, the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes into' alone would put the shot inside the goal, but 'On the contrary' flips it, so the goal word goes inside the shot word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with it means being fashionable and up to date, which is what trendy describes.
